Kyoto event generates approximately US$1.3 million in service revenue for FiEE, highlighting opportunities in next-generation art discovery and collector engagement

OSAKA, Japan, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FiEE, Inc. (NASDAQ: FIEE) ("FiEE" or the "Company"), a technology company integrating Internet of Things ("IoT"), connectivity, and artificial intelligence ("AI") to redefine brand management solutions, today announced the successful completion of its international art exhibition and accompanying auction in Kyoto, Japan. The event marks a milestone in FiEE's evolution toward an online-to-offline ("O2O") ecosystem integrating art and technology ("ArtTech"), connecting artists and global collectors through digital engagement, physical experiences, and commercial transactions.

Organized by the Company's subsidiary, FiEE Channel Limited, in partnership with the Museum of Kyoto, Harmony of Ink: FAx26 Kyoto International Contemporary Art Exchange Exhibition took place from October 23 to 25, 2026. The accompanying auction, held on October 23, 2026, attracted nearly 400 participants online and in person, resulting in an aggregate artwork transaction value of approximately US$2.9 million. The aggregate transaction value represents artwork sales, not the Company's revenue. FiEE generated approximately US$1.3 million in service revenue from the auction, highlighting the commercial potential of its O2O business model. Building on this success, FiEE plans to organize regular art appreciation and networking events to deepen collector engagement and create additional revenue opportunities.

Discovering hidden gems: Engaging the next generation of collectors

FiEE sees opportunities to engage younger collectors, including millennials (Generation Y) and members of Generation Z, who seek originality, cultural identity, and emerging artistic talent beyond established names.

Leveraging its network of key opinion leaders ("KOLs"), digital content capabilities, and curated exhibitions, FiEE aims to connect artists with collectors seeking distinctive artworks and hidden gems. By combining online discovery with physical experiences, the Company seeks to make art more accessible while expanding international exposure for artists.

Beyond transactions: Art advisory as a service

FiEE believes artwork acquisition should mark the beginning of a lasting collector relationship. The Company sees opportunities to develop art advisory services that would offer personalized artwork recommendations, artist introductions, acquisition assistance, collection development, and post-transaction support.

Complementary offerings, including artwork safekeeping, promotional services, and exhibition opportunities, could further strengthen collector relationships. By extending engagement beyond individual purchases, FiEE aims to encourage repeat transactions and generate advisory fees and recurring service revenue, supporting a more diversified business model.

Connecting online discovery with offline experiences

FiEE's O2O strategy integrates digital engagement with physical cultural experiences, creating a connected journey from artwork discovery to acquisition. The Company's software-as-a-service ("SaaS") solutions support this strategy. The FiEE Channel App supports content creation, social media amplification, and audience acquisition, while the Fontree App enables online participation in curated art sales and facilitates transactions. Physical exhibitions and private events are intended to complement these platforms, allowing collectors to experience artworks firsthand and build relationships with artists.

Together, these channels create opportunities for continued engagement, repeat participation, and additional value-added services.

Rafael Li, Chief Executive Officer and President of FiEE, commented, "The success of our Kyoto art exhibition and accompanying auction highlights FiEE's ability to translate digital engagement into meaningful commercial transactions while establishing a foundation for a broader ArtTech ecosystem. We see exciting opportunities among younger collectors seeking hidden gems and emerging talent. By seeking to combine personalized art advisory, curated experiences, and a global collector network, we aim to make art discovery more accessible and rewarding.

"Our vision extends beyond individual transactions. We aim to connect online discovery with offline experiences and build lasting relationships between artists and collectors, with the goal of unlocking new revenue opportunities and creating long-term value for our stockholders."

About FiEE, Inc.

FiEE, Inc. (NASDAQ: FIEE), formerly Minim, Inc., was founded in 1977. It has a historical track record of delivering a comprehensive WiFi/SaaS platform in the market. After years of development, it made the strategic decision to transition to a Software First Model in 2024 to expand its technology portfolio and revenue streams. In 2025, FiEE, Inc. rebranded itself as a technology company leveraging its expertise in IoT, connectivity, and AI to explore new business prospects and extend its global footprint.

FiEE, Inc.'s services are structured into four key categories: Cloud-Managed Connectivity (WiFi) Platform, IoT Hardware Sales & Licensing, SaaS Solutions, and Professional To-C and To-B Services & Support. Notably, FiEE, Inc. has introduced its innovative SaaS solutions, which integrate its AI and data analytics capabilities into content creation and brand management. This initiative has nurtured a robust pool of KOLs on major social media platforms worldwide, helping them develop, manage, and optimize their digital presence. FiEE, Inc.'s services include customized graphics and posts, short videos, and editorial calendars tailored to align with brand objectives.

SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif., Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Nkarta, Inc. (Nasdaq: NKTX), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing engineered natural killer (NK) cell therapies to treat autoimmune diseases, today announced that it will host a webcast on Monday, November 9, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. ET, to review initial clinical data from its Ntrust program evaluating NKX019 in myositis and systemic sclerosis being presented at the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Convergence 2026 in Orlando.

Live Webcast
To access the webcast, please register through this link: https://nkarta-clinical-update-acr-convergence-2026.open-exchange.net/

A replay will be archived on the Investors section of Nkarta’s website, www.nkartatx.com.

About the Ntrust℠ Clinical Trials in Autoimmune Disease
Ntrust-1 (NCT06557265) and Ntrust-2 (NCT06733935) are multi-center, open-label, dose-escalation clinical trials in patients with autoimmune disease receiving lymphodepletion followed by CD19-targeted CAR-NK cell therapy. Both trials assess the safety of NKX019 in people living with autoimmune diseases as well as its potential to achieve durable remission via a “reset” of the immune system through the elimination of pathogenic B cells.  

The Ntrust trials are enrolling up to 12 patients per dose level per disease indication, with leading indications in myositis and systemic sclerosis, as well as ANCA-associated vasculitis, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus nephritis, and primary membranous nephropathy. Additional patients may be enrolled if needed to refine patient populations for further study.

In both studies, patients receive a three-dose cycle of NKX019 following lymphodepletion with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide or cyclophosphamide alone, if they have significant cytopenia at baseline. This approach is designed to evaluate the single-agent activity of NKX019 and facilitate a more rapid path to regulatory approval. Patients in both trials may also receive additional cycles, if needed, to restore response or enable a deeper response.
   
About NKX019
NKX019 is an allogeneic, cryopreserved, off-the-shelf immunotherapy candidate that uses natural killer (NK) cells derived from the peripheral blood of healthy adult donors. It is engineered with a humanized CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) for enhanced cell targeting and a proprietary, membrane-bound form of interleukin-15 (IL-15) for greater persistence and activity without exogenous cytokine support. CD19 is a biomarker for normal B cells as well as those implicated in autoimmune disease. Nkarta is evaluating NKX019 in multiple autoimmune conditions.

About Nkarta
Nkarta is a clinical-stage biotechnology company advancing the development of allogeneic, off-the-shelf natural killer (NK) cell therapies for people living with autoimmune diseases. By harnessing the power of the innate immune system to eliminate pathogenic B cells driving the autoimmune response, Nkarta is advancing novel cell therapies engineered for deep therapeutic impact. The on-demand availability and outpatient dosing of our CAR-NK cells enable a broad population of patients with different autoimmune conditions to conveniently access NK cell therapy in community health settings. Key Terms

fcrnmedical
The neonatal Fc receptor (FCRN or FcRn) is a protein that controls how long antibodies and the blood protein albumin stay in circulation by protecting them from being broken down. For investors, therapies that block or harness FcRn can change a drug’s dosing, effectiveness and market appeal—either by lengthening beneficial antibodies for longer-lasting treatments or by reducing harmful antibodies in autoimmune disease—so progress in FcRn-targeted programs can materially affect a biotech’s commercial value.
igf-1rmedical
A protein on the surface of cells that acts like an antenna for a growth signal called insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1); when IGF-1 binds this receptor, it tells cells to grow and survive. Investors care because many experimental drugs aim to block or modulate this receptor to treat cancers and other diseases, so clinical trial results, regulatory decisions, or safety findings related to IGF-1R can strongly influence a biotech company’s value and risk profile.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 6, 2026) - Telo Genomics Corp. (TSXV: TELO) (OTCQB: TDSGF) (the "Company" or "Telo Genomics"), a leader in the development of diagnostic and prognostic tests based on three-dimensional analysis of telomeres (which are the ends of chromosomes), today announced that it closed a term loan agreement effective October 29, 2026, with BrightArc Capital Adminco 1 Inc. (the "Lender") for a principal amount of $250,000 (the "Term Loan").

The Term Loan is a demand non-revolving facility. The Company has received an initial advance of $100,000, with the balance of the Term Loan to be advanced at a later date. Interest accrues at a simple rate of 1.30% per month (equivalent annual rate of 15.60%), payable monthly in arrears. A minimum of three months of interest is payable if the Term Loan is repaid within three months of advance. The facility is secured by a general security agreement over the Company's present and after-acquired personal property (with specific reference to Scientific Research and Experimental Development ("SR&ED") claims) and an irrevocable assignment of the Company's SR&ED tax credits and refunds. Proceeds are to be used to fund the Company's general operating expenses.

The outstanding balance (principal, accrued interest and other amounts) is due on the earlier of (i) three business days after the Company receives its SR&ED claims for the tax year ended in 2026 or (ii) twelve months from the date of advance. An interest reserve equal to three months of interest is required and may be deducted from the advance. The Term Loan agreement also includes covenants requiring timely filing of SR&ED claims (within 180 days of the Company's June 30 financial year end) and maintenance of direct deposit instructions so that CRA payments are directed to the Lender's account, as well as various negative covenants typical of this type of facility.

About Telo Genomics

Telo Genomics is a biotech company pioneering the most comprehensive telomere platform in the industry with powerful applications and prognostic solutions. These include liquid biopsies and related technologies in oncology and neurological diseases. Liquid biopsy is a rapidly growing field of significant interest to the medical community for being less invasive and more easily replicated than traditional diagnostic approaches. By combining our team's considerable expertise in quantitative analysis of 3D telomeres with molecular biology and artificial intelligence to recognize disease associated genetic instability, Telo Genomics is developing simple and accurate products that improve day-to-day care for patients by serving the needs of pathologists, clinicians, academic researchers and drug developers. The benefits of our proprietary technology have been substantiated in 190+ peer reviewed publications and in 30+ clinical studies involving more than 3,000 patients with multiple cancers and Alzheimer's disease. Our lead application, Telo-MM, is being developed to provide important, actionable information to medical professionals in the treatment of multiple myeloma, a deadly form of blood cancer. PLAINSBORO, N.J. and BAGSVÆRD, Denmark, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Novo Nordisk today announced new real-world data from PLATINUM-Truveta and RHODIUM-2, which are two retrospective studies evaluating associations between semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly injection use versus those not initiating treatment with semaglutide 2.4 mg and liver and cardiometabolic outcomes in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Results were presented at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD), The Liver Meeting® 2026 in Denver, Colorado.

"Living with MASH can be incredibly challenging because the disease may progress without clear symptoms, making it even more important to understand the clinical data about how a treatment may help their disease," said Michelle Skinner Moore, PhD, MBA, Vice President, Medical Affairs at Novo. Both studies were retrospective and observational. Treatment was not randomized, the groups differed in baseline characteristics, and results were based on patients with available follow-up measurements who met treatment-persistence criteria.

Real-world study data can provide valuable insights into how treatments work outside of controlled clinical trial settings. Real-world data analyses also have several limitations; while associations can be demonstrated, causal relationships cannot be definitively established. Results may reflect potential unmeasured confounding, the relatively recent approval of both treatments limited follow-up duration, and electronic medical record data may be subject to coding inaccuracies.

About PLATINUM-Truveta
PLATINUM-Truveta was an observational, retrospective cohort study that used de-identified electronic medical record data from the Truveta database across 30 US health systems from June 2021 through March 2026. Adults with MASH who initiated semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly injection (n=2,873) or resmetirom (n=2,285) were included. Changes from baseline in ALT, AST, body weight, HbA1c, platelets, triglycerides, HDL, and LDL were assessed at three and six months. Patients with prior use of semaglutide or resmetirom, cirrhosis or other chronic liver diseases were excluded, and treatment persistence was required at each time point. To reduce confounding, generalized estimating equations with inverse probability of treatment weighting were applied. Patients in the semaglutide group were defined as having MASH if they had one or more claims with a diagnosis code for MASH (ICD-10 CM K75.81) in the 12 month period before index date.1

About RHODIUM-2
RHODIUM-2 was an observational, retrospective study that used de-identified electronic medical record data from the Truveta database across more than 30 US health systems from June 2021 through March 2026. Adults with MASH were grouped according to whether they initiated semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly injection (n=2,479) or did not initiate semaglutide (n=70,702). Changes from baseline in ALT, AST, body weight, and HbA1c were assessed at 3, 6, and 12 months. Patients with cirrhosis or other liver disease etiologies and those treated with GLP-1 receptor agonists or resmetirom within six months before start of first treatment were excluded. To control for confounding, generalized estimating equations to account for within patient correlation, and inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied.2

About metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH)
MASH is a serious, progressive, metabolic disease affecting the liver, which can be fatal if not managed properly.3 More than 250 million people live with MASH,4 and the number of individuals in advanced stages of the disease is expected to increase over 160% from 2015 to 2030.5 Of those living with overweight or obesity, more than one in three also have MASH.6 And of those currently living with MASH, more than 40% have type 2 diabetes, and more than 8 in 10 also live with obesity.7 People living with MASH often have many other health-related comorbidities,8 such as cardiovascular disease, which is the leading cause of death in people with MASH.9,10

MASH is largely a silent disease due to few and unspecific symptoms in its early stages,3 where nearly 90% of people with MASH remain undiagnosed.11 Once MASH progresses to late stages, there is increased mortality and morbidity, including potential for cirrhosis, liver cancer, and need for liver transplant.12

About semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly injection in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH)
Semaglutide 2.4 mg is a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) FDA-approved under accelerated approval to treat adults with MASH with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring (fibrosis), but not with cirrhosis of the liver, in conjunction with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity.13 This accelerated approval is based on improvement of MASH and liver scarring (fibrosis).13 Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon the verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial.13 Novo is investigating semaglutide 2.4 mg in the ongoing ESSENCE phase 3 trial, evaluating the effect of once weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with MASH with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring (fibrosis) (consistent with stage F2 or F3†).13

It is important to note that semaglutide 2.4 mg injection has a Boxed Warning for possible thyroid tumors, including cancer, and should not be used in those with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN 2). The most common side effects of semaglutide include: nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, stomach (abdomen) pain, changes in skin sensations, headache, tiredness (fatigue), upset stomach, dizziness, feeling bloated, belching, low blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes, gas, stomach flu, heartburn, and hair loss.13

ZUNVEYL’s active metabolite is differentiated from donepezil and rivastigmine in that it binds neuronal nicotinic receptors, most notably the alpha-7 subtype, which is known to have a positive effect on cognition. ALPHA-1062 is also being developed in combination with memantine to treat moderate to severe Alzheimer’s dementia, and as an intranasal formulation for Cognitive Impairment with mTBI.

The expansion to $750.0 million from $550.0 million provides ample liquidity to support the increased size and scope of our business as we continue to move through our growth inflection phase. The new five-year term locks in current attractive terms and is aligned with our identified business needs, potential expansion opportunities, and return of capital initiatives. We thank the syndicate members for their strong participation in our upsized Credit Facility and for their ongoing partnership,” said Anthony Aulicino, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Highlights of the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement

  • Total facility size increased by $200.0 million, for an aggregate Credit Facility of approximately C$ equivalent $750.0 million;
  • Single syndicated revolving credit facility of C$ equivalent $702.0 million, with a co-borrower structure allowing for draws in either Canada or the U.S., in either currency;
  • Canadian-based C$20.0 million operating facility and U.S.-based US$20.0 million operating facility;
  • Accordion feature of C$ equivalent $350.0 million; and
  • Removal of the Total Net Debt to EBITDA covenant and improved non-financial covenant baskets, aligned with the higher credit quality and increased size and scope of the Company.

Celebrating National STEM Day on Nov. 8 by Helping Students Pursue STEM Careers

OAKLAND, Calif., Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The PG&E Corporation Foundation (PG&E Foundation) awarded $327,500 in scholarships to dozens of students pursuing degrees in science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) at colleges and universities across California and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) nationwide.

As communities celebrate National STEM Day on Nov. 8, the PG&E Foundation reaffirms its commitment to building tomorrow's workforce through investments in STEM education and scholarships.

This year, scholarships in the amounts of $2,500, $5,000 and $10,000 are being granted to 57 students from across Pacific Gas and Electric Company's (PG&E) service area through the program.

Since 2012, the Better Together STEM Scholarship Program has awarded nearly $8 million to accomplished students. This contribution is funded by PG&E shareholders and is not recovered through customer rates.

By investing in STEM education, the Foundation helps inspire curiosity, creativity, and innovation while empowering students to develop solutions and technologies that can make a positive impact in their hometown communities and beyond.

Scholarship recipients include Quennel Kempe of Fresno and Caden Kelly of Shingle Springs. Both students attend UC Berkeley. Kempe received a $5,000 scholarship and Kelly received a $2,500 scholarship.

"Receiving the PG&E STEM Scholarship shows me that my community believes in me. The financial assistance and encouragement give me the confidence to achieve my goals and make a greater impact in the future," said Kempe, who is studying computer science. 

"The PG&E STEM Scholarship has given me the freedom to focus fully on my education without the added stress of financial challenges. It also serves as a reminder of the values I want to carry forward, using my education to give back to my community, supporting others and helping make STEM opportunities more accessible for future generations," said Kelly who is studying electrical engineering.

Scholarships are based on academic achievement, demonstrated participation and leadership in school and community activities, and financial need. Recipients may reapply annually for up to five years.

Watch PG&E's video series of past STEM scholar recipients.

"We hope these students discover a path in science, technology, engineering, and math that not only leads to new innovations and breakthroughs but also brings them fulfillment and a sense of purpose. We are proud to support them on their journey as they pursue their higher education goals and dreams," said Carla Peterman, President, PG&E Corporation, and Chair of The PG&E Corporation Foundation Board.

Scholarship recipients must plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study for the entire 2026-2027 academic year and pursue their first undergraduate degree at an accredited four-year institution in California. HBCU eligibility was recently added after an increasing number of applicants were admitted to historically Black colleges and universities, none of which are in California.

Employees Supporting Local Scholars

In addition to the Better Together STEM Scholarship Program, PG&E's 11 employee resource groups (ERGs) and three engineering networking groups (ENGs) award scholarships to help offset the cost of higher education. The funds are raised entirely from employee contributions through direct donations, fundraising events and the company's employee giving program known as Campaign for the Community. Since 1989, more than $6 million ERG/ENG Scholarships has been raised and awarded to thousands of our hometown students.

Pacific Gas and Electric Company, a subsidiary of PG&E Corporation (NYSE: PCG), is a combined natural gas and electric utility serving more than 16 million people across 70,000 square miles in Northern and Central California.
